resources.string: See what changed. Keep it local.
Every update, in one calm place.
Choose a page from the watchlist. Its newest version opens here without taking you away from the rest.
Save the first version to start comparing.
We need at least two saved versions to compare changes.
These two versions were captured with different methods (text vs screenshot), so they can’t be compared directly.
The text content of both versions is identical.
Used by pages that follow the app’s default. Other pages keep their own capture method.
For pages that follow app settings
Wait time before capturing page content
Choose an interval from 15 minutes to 7 days.
Change Detection is built on these projects.
Change Detection checks the pages you choose and keeps a local history you can compare.
Open the page in the built-in browser (or share it from yours), sign in if needed, and pick the parts to watch.
The first successful check saves a starting point. Alerts begin with the next change.
Use battery-friendly background checks for everyday tracking.
You control the interval and network or power requirements.
Use Quick Monitor when timing matters
Check selected pages every %1$d to %2$d seconds for up to 3 hours.
Quick Monitor stops when its timer ends. You can stop it sooner at any time.
Open a page to compare saved versions as text, rendered pages, or screenshots.
Your saved versions and change history stay on your device.
Return to the app to manage your pages and review saved changes.
Try another page name or address.

Keeps up to 100 versions per page. Older versions are removed above 250 MB. Each page’s latest two versions are always kept, even if they exceed this budget.
Each page keeps its latest two versions. %1$s of older versions will be deleted from this device. This can’t be undone.
Switching methods starts a new baseline. Existing history is kept.

Free up storage and try again. Your saved history is kept.
Try again. Your saved history is kept. If it keeps happening, send a report.

This older filter ignores changes below a byte threshold. It compares stored data, not visible pixels. Remove it to use the selected rule without this extra filter.
Edit this page and preview its region rules. The selector may no longer match, or the response may not be HTML. Saved history is kept.
Only matching HTML is saved. Changes outside the region or in ignored elements do not trigger alerts. Preview before saving. Leave the include selector empty to watch the whole page.
Use valid CSS selectors of at most %1$d characters each, without regular-expression selectors.

resources.string: The whole page, as it looks
The site is busy or down. This is usually temporary; we’ll keep trying.
Could not connect to this page. Check the page address and your connection, then try again.
This page needs a sign-in. Screenshot and Text checks reuse the app browser’s sign-in on this device. Source checks cannot.
The page doesn’t exist anymore. Check that the link is still right.
The site is asking us to slow down. Checking less often usually fixes this.
The part you picked isn’t on the page anymore. Pick it again.
The page came back in a way we couldn’t read. Try Screenshot instead.
Something went wrong during the last check. Your history is safe.
Saved %1$s. Changes will show up here.
When a page you watch changes, it shows up here, newest first.
The words on the page are the same. Only hidden parts changed, like scripts or markup.
Tap a version to see what changed compared with the one before it.
Screenshot checks are available on Android and iOS. Choose Text for this page, or check it from the mobile app.
This schedule applies to all active pages. Quick Monitor sessions run on their own and don’t change it.
Android picks the exact moment to save battery, so checks can run a little late. For time‑critical pages, use Quick Monitor.
Alerts, sounds and banners in system settings
Type an address or paste a link to preview what you’ll watch.
This page barely has any text
It probably loads its content with JavaScript, so a text check would miss real changes. A screenshot sees the page the way you do.
Changing what’s watched starts fresh from the next check. Your history stays, and the switch itself won’t send an alert.
Reads the words on the page. Fast and light on battery. Best for prices, dates, job posts and listings.
Compares how the page looks. Catches images, layout and pages built with JavaScript. Slower and uses more data.
Any change in the page’s source counts, including scripts and whitespace. Noisy on most sites.
Compares the page’s HTML after cleanup. Catches markup changes you can’t see.
Follows the default set in Settings.
You pick a page. We check it from this device, keep each version that differs, and show you exactly what changed.
Removed words are struck through in red. New words are highlighted. Nothing else on the page is shown unless you ask.
Made by one person for the things you don’t want to miss. Free, open source, no account, no tracking. Pages are checked from your device, and everything stays on it.
Shows saved page content, which may be private. Android controls lock-screen visibility.
